definition: The displayed or inferred title, heading, or caption that identifies the snapshot.
rationale: Titles are usually the strongest single searchable description of a snapshot’s content and should be normalized across figures, tables, maps, and charts.
sample_fields: table_title, figure_title, snapshot_title, chart_title, map_title, table_caption

definition: A concise description of the main analytical subject or purpose of the snapshot.
rationale: Many snapshots have terse or generic titles; a subject summary improves discovery by describing what the snapshot is substantively about.
sample_fields: table_subject, map_subject, table_topic, analytical_focus, table_purpose, assessment_topic

definition: Broad topical, policy, sectoral, or thematic domains represented by the snapshot.
rationale: Domain facets support browsing across humanitarian, economic, health, education, finance, and policy-report content without relying on exact indicator names.
sample_fields: subject_domain, subject_topic, thematic_domain, subject_area, topic_domain, policy_domain, sector

definition: The structural form used to present the data, such as table, map, line chart, bar chart, dashboard, or composite figure.
rationale: Visualization type helps users filter for reusable analytical forms and understand whether the snapshot supports trend, spatial, categorical, or tabular analysis.
sample_fields: visualization_type, map_type, chart_purpose, statistical_output_type, financial_data_type

definition: The language used in the snapshot text, labels, or title.
rationale: Language enables multilingual indexing, OCR routing, translation workflows, and language-based filtering.
sample_fields: language, snapshot_language, data_language, content_language, source_language, document_language

definition: The document-assigned label, number, annex, exhibit, or map identifier for the snapshot.
rationale: Internal identifiers support citation, cross-reference, navigation, and disambiguation among multiple snapshots in the same document.
sample_fields: figure_number, table_number, figure_identifier, table_identifier, map_identifier, annex_identifier

definition: The title of the PDF or parent document containing the snapshot.
rationale: Parent-document title provides provenance and broader context when a snapshot is indexed independently, especially for project and research outputs.
sample_fields: source_document_title, document_context_title, document_title, parent_document_title, document_context

definition: Organization or institutional unit responsible for publishing, producing, issuing, branding, or reporting the snapshot or source document.
rationale: Organizational provenance supports authority assessment, institutional filtering, and trust evaluation.
sample_fields: source_organization, issuing_organization, publishing_organization, map_producer, reporting_organization, institutional_source

definition: Dataset, survey, monitoring system, citation, provider, URL, or source note from which the snapshot’s data values are derived.
rationale: Data-source metadata is essential for provenance, reproducibility, reliability assessment, and finding snapshots derived from the same underlying source.
sample_fields: source_citation, data_source, data_source_name, source_dataset, source_datasets, data_provider, source_url

definition: Footnotes, caveats, methodological notes, data-quality notes, disclaimers, or rights statements needed to interpret or reuse the snapshot.
rationale: Notes often contain critical exclusions, definitions, preliminary-status caveats, boundary disclaimers, or attribution requirements that are not captured in titles or labels.
sample_fields: data_quality_note, footnote_text, table_note, methodological_note, data_notes, boundary_disclaimer, rights_statement

definition: Year, date range, study period, reporting period, or time span covered by the data.
rationale: Temporal coverage is fundamental for filtering, comparison, trend analysis, and avoiding confusion with document publication dates.
sample_fields: time_period, data_time_period, study_period, fiscal_year_range, comparison_periods, time_points

definition: Point-in-time date associated with the snapshot, reporting status, data vintage, map, or as-of statement.
rationale: Reference dates are critical for time-sensitive humanitarian, financial, operational, and statistical snapshots.
sample_fields: reference_date, as_of_date, reporting_date, snapshot_date, map_date, data_as_of_date, data_reference_date

definition: Frequency or resolution of time observations, such as annual, quarterly, monthly, daily, fiscal year, or survey round.
rationale: Granularity helps determine whether a snapshot supports trend analysis, monitoring, or comparison with other time-series data.
sample_fields: temporal_granularity, temporal_frequency, measurement_frequency, temporal_resolution, time_granularity, data_frequency

definition: Primary country, region, administrative area, or geographic extent to which the snapshot applies.
rationale: Geographic scope is one of the most important discovery facets for institutional data snapshots and enables place-based filtering and comparison.
sample_fields: geographic_scope, country, country_or_region, primary_geographic_context, geographic_reference

definition: Named countries, territories, regions, cities, camps, settlements, or other places represented inside the snapshot.
rationale: Entity-level geographic labels expose place names embedded in tables, charts, and maps that may not appear in document metadata.
sample_fields: geographic_entities, location_names, named_places, geographic_units, countries_or_territories, mapped_locations, territory_names

definition: Spatial or administrative level at which data are reported, such as national, province, district, city, facility, site, or settlement level.
rationale: Granularity helps users assess whether the snapshot supports national comparison, subnational analysis, or site-level reuse.
sample_fields: administrative_level, geographic_granularity, spatial_granularity, geographic_unit_type, location_granularity, geographic_unit

definition: The analytical role played by a geography, such as origin, destination, asylum location, reporting country, comparator, or context geography.
rationale: Distinguishing geographic roles prevents misinterpretation, especially in displacement, migration, trade, and flow data.
sample_fields: geographic_role, country_of_asylum, origin_location, destination_locations, origin_dimension, destination_dimension, geographic_role_dimensions

definition: Type of place, facility, settlement, institution, service point, or mapped feature to which the data apply.
rationale: Location type supports discovery of snapshots about camps, hospitals, schools, transit centers, distribution points, offices, and other operational settings.
sample_fields: facility_type, location_type, service_delivery_point_type, population_site_types, organization_presence_types, primary_mapped_feature

definition: Population, beneficiary, stakeholder, or subject group described by the snapshot.
rationale: Population facets are central for humanitarian, demographic, education, health, and development discovery.
sample_fields: population_group, subject_population, beneficiary_population, affected_population_group, focal_subpopulation, reference_population

definition: Age categories, ranges, or life-stage groups represented or used for disaggregation.
rationale: Age-group metadata supports demographic filtering, equity analysis, and comparison across population snapshots.
sample_fields: age_group, age_range, age_group_categories, demographic_disaggregation

definition: Sex or gender categories represented in the data or used as disaggregation groups.
rationale: Gender metadata supports discovery of sex-disaggregated evidence and equity-focused analysis.
sample_fields: sex_or_gender_group, gender, gender_disaggregation, disaggregation_categories, sex_or_gender

definition: Legal, protection, or administrative status categories used to classify people or cases.
rationale: Legal-status categories are key facets for refugee, asylum, protection, and rights-monitoring data.
sample_fields: legal_status_categories, population_status_categories, population_group_categories, current_status_category

definition: Displacement, migration, or residency status of the represented population.
rationale: Displacement status enables humanitarian filtering for refugees, IDPs, returnees, stateless persons, host communities, and other affected groups.
sample_fields: displacement_status, settlement_status_indicator, self_settled_status, movement_type, movement_context

definition: Name of the indicator, variable, metric, outcome, or measured concept represented in the snapshot.
rationale: Indicator names are the core semantic content needed for fine-grained search and analytical reuse.
sample_fields: indicator_name, indicator_names, primary_indicator, outcome_indicators, measured_variable, chart_indicator_names

definition: Text explaining how an indicator, variable, category, or measure is defined, coded, or operationalized.
rationale: Definitions improve interpretability and prevent false matches between similarly named indicators.
sample_fields: indicator_definition, indicator_description, variable_definition, variable_definitions, category_definitions, abbreviation_definitions

definition: Name of the quantitative measure or value column reported in the snapshot.
rationale: Measure names distinguish costs, counts, percentages, budgets, disbursements, coefficients, rates, and other numeric quantities.
sample_fields: measure_name, measure_names, measure_column, measure_labels, value_measure, financial_measure_names

definition: Unit used to interpret numeric values, such as percent, people, households, kilometers, index points, or monetary units.
rationale: Units are essential for comparing and reusing quantitative data correctly.
sample_fields: unit_of_measure, measurement_unit, indicator_units, x_axis_unit_of_measure, y_axis_unit_of_measure, scale_unit

definition: Currency denomination, currency code, or monetary unit used for financial values.
rationale: Currency metadata prevents misinterpretation of monetary figures and supports comparison across financial snapshots.
sample_fields: currency, currency_code, currency_unit, monetary_unit

definition: Statistical or quantitative form of the values, such as count, share, percentage distribution, rate, average, total, index, coefficient, or amount.
rationale: Measure type helps users distinguish raw counts from normalized, proportional, modeled, or summary values.
sample_fields: measure_type, value_type, statistic_type, statistical_measure, metric_type, measurement_type

definition: Conceptual dimension represented by table rows or row groups.
rationale: Row dimensions expose the structure of tabular data and make row-level categories reusable for search and analysis.
sample_fields: row_dimension, row_labels, row_category_labels, row_categories, row_group_labels, subrow_dimension

definition: Conceptual dimension represented by table columns or column groups.
rationale: Column dimensions clarify whether values are organized by time, geography, group, measure, model, funding source, or other variables.
sample_fields: column_dimension, column_dimensions, column_headers, column_labels, column_categories

definition: Main categorical variable used to group, classify, or organize values in the snapshot.
rationale: Category dimensions describe what entities, statuses, groups, or classes are being compared across charts, tables, and maps.
sample_fields: category_dimension, categorical_dimension, classification_dimension, category_type, primary_dimension

definition: Observed labels for categories, classes, row values, column values, bins, statuses, or groups.
rationale: Category labels expose searchable semantic content that often appears only inside the visual object.
sample_fields: category_labels, category_values, column_category_labels, row_category_labels, outcome_category_labels, x_axis_categories

definition: Dimension represented by separate plotted series, legend entries, lines, bars, or repeated measures.
rationale: Series dimensions clarify what is being compared within a visualization and support reuse of multi-series charts.
sample_fields: series_dimension, series_labels, series_values, data_series_labels, grouping_variable

definition: Names or labels of individual data series, legend items, or plotted measures.
rationale: Series labels make embedded chart content discoverable by specific comparator, indicator, scenario, or group.
sample_fields: series_labels, series_label, data_series_names, chart_series_labels, legend_labels, series_names

definition: Dimension by which indicators are broken down for subgroup, equity, spatial, demographic, or categorical analysis.
rationale: Disaggregation dimensions support discovery of gender, age, wealth, location, refugee-host, sector, and other subgroup analyses.
sample_fields: disaggregation_dimension, disaggregation_dimensions, breakdown_dimension, demographic_dimensions, socioeconomic_disaggregation

definition: Benchmark, peer group, comparator country, region, income group, treatment group, or other entity used for comparison.
rationale: Comparison groups reveal benchmarking context and help users find snapshots suitable for comparative analysis.
sample_fields: comparison_groups, comparison_group, comparison_entities, benchmark_labels, comparison_geographies, comparison_group_labels

definition: Variable, indicator, dimension, or measure represented along a chart axis.
rationale: Axis variables are essential for interpreting plotted relationships when axis labels contain substantive concepts not in the title.
sample_fields: x_axis_dimension, y_axis_variable, x_axis_indicator, y_axis_indicator, y_axis_measure, axis_value_range

definition: Method, instrument, program, registration process, assessment, or monitoring mechanism used to collect or verify the data.
rationale: Collection-method metadata supports provenance, comparability, and filtering by surveys, monitoring systems, audits, registration methods, and consultations.
sample_fields: data_collection_method, data_collection_instrument, assessment_type, assessment_or_data_collection, data_collection_program, data_collection_or_registration_method

definition: Method used to calculate, derive, weight, simulate, estimate, or transform reported values.
rationale: Calculation metadata distinguishes direct observations from modeled, weighted, simulated, or author-derived estimates.
sample_fields: calculation_method, calculation_note, data_derivation_method, measurement_method, aggregation_statistic

definition: Statistical, econometric, modeling, analytical, or evaluative method underlying the snapshot.
rationale: Method metadata enables discovery of regression tables, simulations, structural-break tests, cost-effectiveness analyses, and other analytical outputs.
sample_fields: analysis_method, analytical_method, statistical_method, estimation_method, analysis_type, analytical_tool

definition: Dependent variable, outcome, result, or main effect being estimated, measured, or explained.
rationale: Outcome-variable metadata is central for finding analytical tables by the substantive result being modeled or evaluated.
sample_fields: outcome_variable, dependent_variable, dependent_variables, outcome_variables, model_outcome_variables, outcome_indicator

definition: Name of the project, program, operation, response plan, initiative, or fund associated with the snapshot.
rationale: Project names connect snapshot-level evidence to institutional operations and enable project-level discovery across documents.
sample_fields: project_name, project_context, parent_project_name, project_or_program_names, program_or_plan_names

definition: Formal identifier for a project, operation, loan, credit, or institutional project record.
rationale: Identifiers enable precise linking between extracted snapshots, project databases, and related documents.
sample_fields: project_identifier, project_id, document_project_id, operation_identifier

definition: Project component, subcomponent, results area, workstream, or component identifier represented in the snapshot.
rationale: Component metadata supports retrieval of costs, indicators, and activities by project structure.
sample_fields: project_component, component_name, component_identifier, project_component_categories, subcomponent_categories

definition: Assistance modality, service, program activity, policy intervention, treatment, or operational action represented or evaluated.
rationale: Intervention metadata supports thematic discovery of snapshots about food assistance, vaccination, cash transfers, procurement, reforms, services, and other program activities.
sample_fields: intervention_type, assistance_type, service_type, service_or_intervention, policy_intervention, intervention_area

definition: Organization, donor, funding window, institution, or source category providing or associated with financing.
rationale: Financing-source metadata enables donor tracking, lender filtering, and discovery of project-finance tables.
sample_fields: financing_source, funding_source, funding_agency, selected_financing_sources, financing_source_categories

definition: Type or modality of financing, such as loan, credit, grant, guarantee, equity, trust fund, or financing window.
rationale: Financing instrument supports comparison of financial structures across project appraisal and portfolio snapshots.
sample_fields: financing_instrument, financing_type, financial_instrument_type, financial_instrument_types, funding_type

definition: Financial, budgetary, cost, disbursement, funding-gap, economic-value, or portfolio measure represented in the snapshot.
rationale: Financial metrics are core searchable concepts for project finance, humanitarian funding, procurement, and economic appraisal tables.
sample_fields: financial_metric, financial_metrics, financial_measure_type, funding_amount, disbursement_values, financing_gap_status
